story_type: unarmed ICBM test launch erupting out of an underground silo, launch keys turned, historic film
hook: Seven thousand miles of range, fired out of a hole.
narration: This missile could strike more than seven thousand miles away, and it launched out of a hole in the ground.
It was Minuteman Two, America's most advanced intercontinental ballistic missile, in testing at the Cape in 1965.
A Minuteman waits sealed in an underground silo, ready to fly within minutes, which is where the name comes from.
Test shots flew from the Cape to a target near Ascension Island, five thousand miles away.
The crew counted down, turned the switches, and the silo erupted.
outcome: Seven Minuteman missiles were fired from the Cape in 1965, and every one of them was successful.
title: Minuteman fired out of a silo
question_comment: Could you have been the one to turn that switch?

facts.claim: Minuteman 2, most advanced ICBM, testing in 1965
facts.source_quote: Minute Man 2, America's most advanced intercontinental ballistic missile, continued testing during 1965.
SAC's operational version will have a striking range of over 7,000 miles.

facts.claim: Target near Ascension Island, about 5,000 miles
facts.source_quote: At the Eastern Test Range, the missile is fired to a target area near Ascension Island, approximately 5,000 miles away.
Seven minute-man missiles were fired during 1965. All were successful.

description:
A Minuteman II intercontinental ballistic missile test is launched from an underground silo at Cape Kennedy, Florida, during 1965, when all seven Minuteman test shots from the Cape were successful.
